Wibaux soils are characteristic of steep scoria hills, and recovery may also often be limited by excessive slopes on which equipment cannot operate. Tract II is dominated by loam and silty clay loam soils, while textures of soils on Tract III are primarily loam and fine sandy loam.
Chemical limitations of topsoil associated with a soil series have not been identified within Tracts II and III. Saline conditions have been identified low in the profile at two of 41 locations sampled on Tract III; these were within disturbed Thedalund-Wibaux complex and Chugter loam mapping units. The disturbed Thedalund-Wibaux soil also had a high boron level. Based on data collected on Tract III, chemical limitations are uncommon, irregular in occurrence and where present, low in the profile.
Overburden and Interburden Characteristics - Westmoreland Resources has drilled 38 holes on Tract III and 11 holes on Tract III for the purpose of studying chemical characteristics of overburden and interburden materials. Interburden is the material between the Rosebud-McKay and Robinson seams, and overburden is the material overlying the Rosebud-McKay seam, or in the case of single seam coal, the Robinson seam.

Drill hole material was analyzed in stratigraphic intervals generally of 10 feet or less; on the average 20 or more samples per hole were analyzed. Results and interpretations of chemical data are presented in detail in reports prepared by the Colorado School of Mines Research Institute (1975 a and 1975 b).
